summary: Mississippi Forestry Commission 100 ft Aermotor tower near Wilmot, completed by Oct 1961; NHLR 2022 site visit says site appears privately owned.

facts.design: 100 ft Aermotor tower with a small cabin on top
facts.status_note: Last documented at the NHLR site visit of July 8, 2022; present condition not confirmed in sources read.

access.note: NHLR says the site appears to be privately owned. Do not encourage visits.

events.note: Completed by October 1961, per a Delta Democrat item dated October 18, 1961, reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register July 10, 2022

evidence.supports: Cabin with glass windows and swing-up trapdoor on top, per 1961 item
evidence.quote: the little glass-windower cabin established on top with a swing-up trapdoor

evidence.supports: Erected by Mississippi Forestry Commission, completed by 1961 item
evidence.quote: The new forest fire lookout tower erected by the Mississippi Forestry Commission on the road between Wilmot and the Swiftwater Church, has been completed

evidence.supports: Planned use November to March to spot fires across the county
evidence.quote: It will be used during fire season, November-March, to spot fires throughout Washington County.
This site appears to be privately owned

evidence.supports: 1961 item and Forest Lookouts page use Wilmot
evidence.quote: between Wilmot and the Swiftwater Church

evidence.supports: NHLR gives build date as unknown

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR leaves the build date unknown; the October 1961 item shows the tower completed by then. The story uses 1961 as the completion date.

notes_for_editor: Name: NHLR uses 'Wilmont' and the brief lists 'Wilmot' as another name; the 1961 item and the Forest Lookouts page use 'Wilmot'. The editor may want the display name changed; no correction was recorded. The 1961 date comes from a secondary site quoting the Delta Democrat; the original clipping on newspapers.com returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The 'standing' status is only shown as of the 7/8/22 NHLR site visit. NHLR says the site appears privately owned, so visits should not be encouraged.
